what_its_for: Tropicamide is an eye drop used to widen (dilate) your pupils and temporarily relax the muscles in your eye. Your eye doctor uses it during eye exams to get a better look at the back of your eye, including your retina and optic nerve. It may also be used before certain eye procedures or to help treat some eye conditions.
how_to_take: Wash your hands well before using these eye drops. Tilt your head back, pull down your lower eyelid to make a small pocket, and place the prescribed number of drops into that pocket. Gently close your eye for 1 to 2 minutes — try not to blink or squeeze your eye shut. Press lightly on the inner corner of your eye (near your nose) with your finger for about 1 minute to help keep the medicine in your eye. If you wear contact lenses, remove them before using the drops and ask your doctor when it is safe to put them back in. Do not let the tip of the dropper touch your eye, fingers, or any surface to keep it clean.
dosing: Your eye doctor will decide the exact dose and how many drops to use. Usually, 1 to 2 drops are placed in the affected eye or eyes. For an eye exam, the drops are typically given about 15 to 20 minutes before the exam. The effects last for several hours. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as the dose may be adjusted based on your needs.
missed_dose: Tropicamide is most often given in the doctor's office right before an eye exam, so you are unlikely to miss a dose. If you have been given these drops to use at home on a schedule and you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not use extra drops to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store tropicamide eye drops at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Protect the drops from light and heat. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children. Do not use the drops if they look cloudy, discolored, or have particles in them. Check the expiration date on the label and discard the bottle if it has expired.
what_to_avoid: After receiving these eye drops, your vision will be blurry and your eyes will be very sensitive to light for several hours. Do NOT drive a car or operate heavy machinery until your vision has fully returned to normal. Wear sunglasses outdoors to protect your eyes from bright light and reduce discomfort. Avoid touching or rubbing your eyes. Children and older adults should be watched carefully after using these drops, as they may be more sensitive to the effects.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: severe eye pain, very red eyes, sudden vision changes or loss of vision, seeing halos around lights, nausea or vomiting along with eye pain (these could be signs of increased eye pressure), a fast or irregular heartbeat, flushing, dry mouth, confusion, difficulty urinating, or a severe allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of your face or throat, or trouble breathing. These side effects are rare but require immediate attention.
when_it_works: The eye drops usually start to work within 15 to 30 minutes after being placed in the eye. Your pupils will be at their widest about 20 to 40 minutes after the drops are given. The blurry vision and light sensitivity caused by the drops typically last anywhere from 4 to 8 hours, but in some people — especially children — the effects may last longer. Your vision should return to normal on its own without any additional treatment.
special_populations: Children: Children are more sensitive to tropicamide and may be more likely to have side effects such as fast heartbeat, flushing, or fever. Use only as directed by your doctor. Older Adults: Older patients may be at higher risk for increased eye pressure (a condition called angle-closure glaucoma) after using this medication. Tell your doctor if you have ever been told you have narrow-angle glaucoma. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before using these drops. The safety of tropicamide during pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been fully established. People with certain health conditions: Let your doctor know if you have glaucoma, an enlarged prostate, urinary problems, heart disease, high blood pressure, or thyroid disease, as tropicamide may need to be used with extra caution or may not be appropriate for you.
